Consultation

Board seeks views on standard industrial meter checks

Opened: 7 October 2026

Closes: 1 November 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has opened a consultation on minimum checks for industrial electricity meter accounts. Proposals cover verification of meter multipliers when an account is created, transferred or changed following electrical work.

The Board is seeking evidence from suppliers, meter technicians and industrial customers about current checking practices and the cost of keeping verification records.

Consultation

Views invited on clearer gas maintenance spending records

Opened: 28 August 2026

Closes: 28 September 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has opened a consultation on the records gas network operators submit to support maintenance costs. The proposed template links each claimed amount to a job reference, completion record and invoice or staff time entry.

The consultation asks whether these fields provide enough evidence without duplicating existing records. Written responses are accepted through the Board's consultation form.

News release

Amberford electricity connection delays prompt formal improvement notice

Published: 6 October 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has issued a formal improvement notice to the Amberford electricity network operator after an audit found repeated delays in providing connection quotations. Of 160 complete applications examined, 47 had not received a quotation within the required 15 working days.

The applications covered small shops, workshops and housing developments. The longest recorded wait was 38 working days. The operator attributed the backlog to vacancies and incomplete internal handovers. The Board found that these problems did not remove its obligation to meet the published service standard.

The notice requires weekly reporting of outstanding quotations and a named contact for every affected applicant. It also requires the operator to separate applications awaiting customer information from those delayed within its own teams. The notice imposes no financial penalty. Applicants can ask the operator for a written explanation of their case and use the Board's complaints route if it remains unresolved.

News release

Board clarifies billing rules following household tariff reduction

Published: 17 September 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has issued billing guidance following the household electricity standing charge reduction on 15 September. The guidance addresses questions received from customers and suppliers about bills covering days on both sides of the change. It does not introduce another tariff change.

For a bill covering 1 to 30 September, suppliers must charge 14 days at KRN 0.84 and 16 days at KRN 0.79. The standing charge for that period is therefore KRN 24.40. Electricity used during the period remains subject to the unchanged unit rate of KRN 0.246 per kilowatt hour.

Customers using advance credit meters are also entitled to the lower standing charge from 15 September. Where a meter update has taken longer, suppliers must credit the difference. The Board has asked suppliers to keep records of these adjustments so its billing team can check that customers receive the full reduction.

News release

Board publishes annual review of electricity network charges

Published: 20 August 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has published its annual review of electricity network charges. The review covers the cost of carrying power to homes and businesses across Kestria. It records KRN 184 million in allowed network revenue for the year ended 30 June, against actual spending of KRN 179 million.

Most of the difference came from delayed cable replacement in Amberford and lower maintenance costs around Saltmarsh. The Board has required network operators to explain how the unspent allowance is recorded in their accounts. Operators cannot treat money allowed for unfinished work as an unrestricted surplus.

The review does not change customer tariffs. It also reports that average electricity interruptions fell from 74 minutes to 68 minutes per customer over the year. Rural districts west of Ostara remained above that average, at 112 minutes. The full review includes separate spending and service tables for each network area.

News release

Electricity tariff decision reduces standard household standing charge

Published: 15 September 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has approved a reduction in the standard household electricity standing charge from KRN 0.84 to KRN 0.79 a day. The decision applies from today to customers on the regulated standard tariff. The electricity unit rate remains KRN 0.246 per kilowatt hour.

The reduction reflects lower verified costs for billing and customer account administration. For a household remaining on the tariff for a full 365 days, the standing charge difference is KRN 18.25. Actual bills still depend on consumption, meter readings and any separate credits or charges shown on the account.

Suppliers must show the revised standing charge clearly and divide billing periods where they cross the change date. Customers do not need to apply for the reduction. The Board examined cost returns from all six licensed household suppliers before reaching its decision. Network charges are unchanged by this ruling.

News release

Gas network ruling disallows unsupported maintenance costs

Published: 30 September 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has disallowed KRN 1.8 million of maintenance costs claimed by the Saltmarsh gas network operator. The ruling follows a review of expenditure for the year ended 30 June. The operator did not provide sufficient work records to support costs assigned to 23 maintenance jobs.

The disputed amount forms part of a KRN 41.6 million maintenance claim. The Board accepted KRN 39.8 million after checking invoices, inspection records and staff time entries. The disallowed costs cannot be recovered through regulated network charges. This decision does not alter the tariff currently shown on customer bills.

The ruling concerns evidence supporting expenditure. It makes no finding that the maintenance itself was unnecessary or that the network is unsafe. The operator must keep clearer records linking each charge to completed work. A summary of the assessment explains the evidence requirements and lists the categories of costs that were excluded.

News release

Industrial gas users in Ostara receive pressure advisory

Published: 22 September 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has issued a supply advisory for large gas users connected to the East Ostara industrial branch. A pressure regulator fault identified this morning has reduced the branch's available capacity from 92 to 76 megawatt hours per hour. Household gas connections are unaffected.

The network operator has contacted the 14 sites holding interruptible supply agreements on the branch. Under those agreements, affected sites must keep within the individual limits stated in their notices. The Board has confirmed that the combined reduction requested from these sites is 16 megawatt hours per hour.

Engineering staff are assessing the faulty equipment. No loss of gas containment has been reported. Other industrial customers should continue to follow their existing supply terms and should not change equipment settings on the basis of this advisory alone. The Board's industrial supply desk is recording operational difficulties reported by affected sites.

News release

Ostara industrial gas restrictions lifted after equipment repairs

Published: 29 September 2026

Supply restrictions on the East Ostara industrial gas branch have been lifted following repairs to a pressure regulator. The Kestria Energy Board confirmed the change after reviewing test records supplied by the network operator. The branch has returned to its normal available capacity of 92 megawatt hours per hour.

The restrictions affected 14 sites with interruptible supply agreements from 22 September. The operator recorded a total requested reduction of 16 megawatt hours per hour during the restriction period. It has reported no interruption to household supplies and no loss of gas containment associated with the equipment fault.

Affected businesses have received individual notices cancelling their temporary limits. The Board has requested maintenance records and an explanation of how the fault developed. This review is separate from the decision to restore capacity. Businesses disputing a charge connected with the restriction should first use their supplier's complaints process and retain their meter records.
